name: Year 1 cruise ship Zodiac/VIP mixed-class examination

timing.schedule_ambiguity: Printed source p40 says fourth calendar day (with first day free), while teacher example p41 and narrator p46 refer to the end of a three-day test. Preserve without silently reconciling calendar labels.

outcomes.label: FINAL_CORRECT_GROUP_ANSWER
outcomes.trigger: Earliest valid final-window group response identifies its VIP correctly

outcomes.label: NO_VALID_FINAL_CORRECT_IDENTIFICATION
outcomes.trigger: No qualifying final answer, or wrong final answer by eligible non-VIP outside VIP's class

outcomes.label: EARLY_CORRECT_TRAITOR
outcomes.trigger: Non-VIP student from a different class submits correct early VIP identification

outcomes.label: EARLY_INCORRECT_TRAITOR
outcomes.trigger: Non-VIP student from a different class submits incorrect early VIP identification

critical_validations: Early attempted answers from VIP's classmates do not count and do not terminate
Only first qualifying answer determines group outcome
School mail cannot be copied, transferred, forged or modified
VIP identity and answer submitter remain undisclosed in published result
Class point outcomes do not imply private point balances transfer between classes
Teacher statements regarding timing should not silently override printed source inconsistency
prohibited_actions: Threatening someone to obtain secret VIP data
Submitting from another student's phone without permission
Illicit cross-class communications outside allowed process (source refers to prohibitions, scope pending full normative review)
sanctions: Serious violations including expulsion per briefing; do not model blanket automatic expulsion without procedure
anonymity: School publishes group outcome and class delta, not identities; temporary private-point IDs and split receipts mentioned

epistemic_disclosures.knowledge: Vacation expectation, no known test outcome or VIP
Rules and own group roster, not global VIP identities
Whether personal VIP chosen; classmates cannot assume receipt content
Local words and visible device actions; secret SIM changes and betrayal identities not automatically known
Karuizawa identity and layered device switch are understood by a limited set in different ways
Group outcomes and class totals but not hidden VIP identities or traitor submitters as official disclosure

open_questions: School-issued algorithm still not disclosed. V5 provides Suzune's source-backed ordinal pattern but not official certification.
All 12 group rosters and VIP identities not officially disclosed in source
Interaction of prohibited cross-class communication and attending scheduled mixed groups needs full normative wording verification
Calendar day three versus day four source wording conflict
Private-point totals do not disclose each actual receiver's identity
What concrete school procedure applies to coercion and misuse of phone evidence
How discretionary instructor placement of class representatives interacts with criteria for other group members remains unspecified.
The 4.5 account provides no complete VIP role selection algorithm; Suzune's suspicion of Kushida is explicitly unproven.
simulation_policy: REFERENCE_ONLY: Requires a separate verified executable ExamSpec, knowledge fences, timing semantics and operator release before any Zodiac/VIP runtime.

group_assignment_discretion.statement: Hoshinomiya says she deliberately moved Ichinose from Dragon to Rabbit as a challenge; Mashima states there is no rule against her decision. This neither establishes unconstrained instructor authority nor solves VIP allocation.

later_revelations.comment: Horikita suspects Kushida leaked Dragon's VIP but has no proof; Karuizawa privately expects 500000 Rabbit VIP points in September, not yet credited.
Suzune proposes alphabetic surname ordinal linked to Zodiac group animal; Rabbit and Dragon examples match, but school has not formally certified its method.

vip_ordinal_pattern_v05.proposed_rule: Within each named group sort by surname alphabetically and use animal's zodiac rank as 1-based position
vip_ordinal_pattern_v05.scope: Two explicitly exemplified matches; do not assert official deterministic assignment without more normative evidence
